incident-bot: PagerDuty: INCIDENT fired -> service=edge-network | symptom=TLS handshake errors + LB target unavailable in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Link: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/INC12345

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty triggered by monitor "edge-tls-handshake-fail-rate". Priority: P1. Escalation policy: edge-network-oncall. Pager: Amber (oncall). Auto-escalate in 5m if no ack.

Amber (oncall): Acked. Reading details. Observed spike in TLS handshake 525 errors across two regions. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/obs/edge/handshake

Amber (oncall): Quick check — is this only client-facing TLS or internal LB health too? Anyone seeing LB target health flaps?

Raj (netops): I'm seeing TargetGroup/edge-backend in eu-west-1 showing 40/80 healthy -> unhealthy state change ~09:09 UTC. Connection errors: "ERR_TLS_HANDSHAKE": logs show cipher negotiation failures from multiple clients.

Lina (infra): Confirmed. ALB access logs show upstream 504/520 patterns + TLS errors. On my end now: some backends are failing health check "200 OK" because the health path /_hc returns 502.

Marta (sre): Impact estimate from synthetic: 3.6% of requests returned handshake/failure across EU and APAC. US less affected but a small bump in retransmits. Customer-facing pages: some customers reporting 502s to API endpoints.

Amber (oncall): Ok. Raj please run `dig` and check DNS TTLs; could be a propagation TTL change? Also check if any recent cert rotations.

Raj (netops): Running dig now:
```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 edge.redwood.ai A +noall +answer
edge.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 3.22.11.45
edge.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 18.197.12.8
```
TTL is 300. No obvious mispointing. No cert rotation in last 24h per cert rotation log.

Lina (infra): Dumping ALB target health:
```
TargetId t-abc123 state=unhealthy last_status=502 last_failed=09:08:52
TargetId t-def456 state=unhealthy last_status=TLSError last_failed=09:09:14
```
Looks like a subset of backends failing TLS handshake to upstream services (internal service cert mismatch?)

Marta (sre): PagerDuty note: If no mitigation within 10m it will auto-escalate to platform lead. We should consider failover to standby pool and reduce connection reuse for affected backends.

Amber (oncall): Action plan: 1) Raj: check DNS cache (CloudFront + edge caches) and flush if needed. 2) Lina: shift traffic off unhealthy targets (set weight=0 on ALB target group or register backup pool). 3) Marta: open shortblast to CS with impact note.

Raj (netops): Purging our internal DNS cache (consul/edge-dns): `consul kv delete edge/dns/cache` -> kicked. Also requested TTL be reduced to 60 for 10m via infra runbook.

Lina (infra): Running target weight update:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=weight,Value=0 --region eu-west-1
```
Swapped ~50% traffic to standby pool in eu-west-1. Observing decreased error rate.

Amber (oncall): Verified customer impact dashboard: error rate dropped from 3.6% -> 0.8% after weights adjusted. Still seeing TLS errors from a small cohort. Keeping page open. :eyes:

Marta (sre): Sending CS blurb:
"We're investigating intermittent TLS handshake failures affecting a small percentage of traffic in EU/APAC. We've initiated failover to standby backends; impact is degraded but improving. Will follow up in 30m." :email:

Raj (netops): Note: upstream service cert presented chain missing intermediate in some deployments — I'm opening a ticket with infra-cert team. In the meantime, we can enable TLS fallback/cipher relaxation on affected proxies for short window.

Lina (infra): Temporarily relaxed cipher suites on proxy (edge-proxy config roll): `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` added back. Roll applied to 30% -> monitoring.

Amber (oncall): Good. We'll keep monitoring. Marta please own post-incident notes and include runbook gap: cert distribution validation and automated health-check for TLS chain.

pagerduty-bot: Amber (oncall) acknowledged INC12345. Next escalation scheduled in 00:05:00 if not resolved.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied (traffic shifted, DNS cache purge, cipher relaxation). Recommended followup: full cert re-deploy and health-check sweep. Closing timeline pending verification. :white_check_mark:

Raj (netops): FYI I logged ticket INF-2026 for cert reissue to enforce full chain and automated smoke tests.

Amber (oncall): Wrapping up here. I'll keep thread open until 11:15 UTC for verification. If anyone wants to add notes for postmortem, drop them here.

Lina (infra): Adding config snippets to runbook after this. :memo:

Marta (sre): Acknowledged. Preparing timeline + impact numbers for postmortem.
